messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 42 omitted, sha256 6cd0c1665fefd68f>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Entailment
confidence: 70
reason: Section 5c bars each party from soliciting the other's employees, contractors, and affiliated resources, which overlap with the agreement's definition of representatives, so the hypothesis is supported though its wording is vague.
<quote check="exact">each party agrees not to solicit or recruit any employee of each other without the prior written consent of that party</quote>
<quote check="exact">will not solicit for hire, in any capacity whatsoever, any of each other’s employees, contractors or other such affiliated resources</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Entailment
confidence: 82
reason: The NDA bars each party from soliciting the other's employees, contractors and affiliated resources, which fall within the definition of representatives (employees, contractors, advisors, consultants).
<quote check="exact">Both BCG and Partner hereby agree that it will not solicit for hire, in any capacity whatsoever, any of each other’s employees, contractors or other such affiliated resources without prior written consent from the other party.</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Entailment
confidence: 90
reason: The non-solicitation clause bars each party from soliciting the other's employees and contractors, who fall within the agreement's definition of representatives.
<quote check="exact">each party agrees not to solicit or recruit any employee of each other without the prior written consent of that party.</quote>
<quote check="exact">it will not solicit for hire, in any capacity whatsoever, any of each other’s employees, contractors or other such affiliated resources without prior written consent from the other party.</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label":"Entailment","confidence":88,"quotes":["will not solicit for hire, in any capacity whatsoever, any of each other’s employees, contractors or other such affiliated resources"],"reason":"Section 5c bars each party from soliciting the other's employees and contractors, who are among the agreement's defined representatives."}
